8.sourceText:
We normally use simple present tense to talk about countries and nationalities. Not only the verb to be can be useful to talk about this. Revise the following chart and check some examples.
Even when we talk about this topic, the grammar rules must be respected. To Be – works alone. Other verbs – Use auxiliaries.
MOST COMMON QUESTIONS - Where are you from? - Where do you come from?
To Be verb Other verbs – Auxiliary Introduction John is American Is he American? She comes from England. Does she come from England? They are from Mexico Where are they from? You speak Italian Do you speak Italian? The verb to be is an independent verb it can say a sentence, it can make a question or deny by itself. NO AUXILIARY NEEDED The rest of the verbs are dependent. They use auxiliaries to make questions and to deny an action. Do - I/You/We/They Does - He/She/ It (3rd person singular) *Pronunciation hint: https://youtu.be/EMWmCb1CIdc
https://youtu.be/EMWmCb1CIdc

It is common to use the simple present tense to talk about routines; also, the use of adverbs of frequency is common on this topic.
ADVERBS OF FREQUENCY 100% Always We always work at night. 90% Usually She is usually late. 80% Normally They normally go to the beach on Saturdays 70% Often I am often at home. 50% Sometimes You sometimes laugh out loud. 30% Occasionally He occasionally cleans his room. 10% Seldom It seldom rains here. 5% Hardly ever Carol hardly ever takes a call. 0% Never John is never on time.
HINT 1. Adverbs go before verbs since they modify them, EXCEPT for To Be. She is always happy 2. NEVER has a negative connotation. (no need for don’t/doesn’t) They never visit me. 3. Adverbs can work in statements, negative sentences and questions.

It is common to use the simple present tense to talk about jobs and occupations as we saw on the useful language before.
To Be verb Other verbs – Auxiliary Introduction John is a doctor Is he a doctor? John makes shoes. What does John do? They are bakers What is their job? I work as a store manager. work – works stop – stops
wash – washes teach – teaches
study – studies copy – copies

10.sourceText:
We normally use simple present tense to talk about food. Check out the following examples.
STATEMENTS QUESTIONS NEGATIVE STATEMENTS 1. There is one apple on the table. Is there one apple on the table? There isn’t an apple on the table. 2. There are a lot of eggs in the basket. Are there a lot of eggs in the basket? There aren’t any of eggs in the basket. 3. I have some water in the bottle. Do you have any water in the bottle? I don’t have any water in the bottle. To consider: 1. We use the expressions There is (singular) / there are (plural) to say something exists. 2. We can use other verbs to talk about food. See example number 3. 3. When we talk about food, we need to talk about quantity. We use containers and quantifiers: Some – Any – a lot of – Few / A few - None – lots of – Much - Many. Also, there are two main questions when we talk about quantities: How much – Used for uncountable nouns. How much milk is there left? How many – Used for countable nouns. How many do you have?

TO CONSIDER - This / that (singular) These / Those (plural) are demonstratives we use to talk about possessions. This / These (close objects) – That / Those (far objects) - Whose: wh word used to ask for possessions: Whose USB is this? - Possessive adjectives can also be used to talk about belongings: This is my house. - Every possessive adjective has a possessive pronoun: My / Mine, Your / yours, His / His, Her / Hers, Its / Its, Our / Ours, Their / Theirs (used when we already know what we are talking about) - Demonstrative pronouns can also work as adjectives. E.G That house is blue. Let’s watch the video on the platform.
We normally use simple present tense to talk about belongings. Check out the following examples.
Statements Questions Negative Statements 1. This is Joe’s car. Is this Joe’s car? / Whose car is this? This is not Joe’s car. 2. That is our house. Is that your house? / Whose house is that? That is not ours. 3. These are my keys. Are these your keys? / Whose keys are these? These are not mine. 4. Those are Mary’s children. Are those Mary’s children? / Whose Children are those? No, those aren’t Mary’s.

8.sourceText:
We normally talk about places and we include the use of adjectives to describe their characteristics. Adjectives are words we use to denote specificities about people, places or situations.
Statements Questions Negative statements 1. Mexico has the ancient ruins of the Mayas Does Mexico have the ancient ruins of the Mayas? No, it does not have the ancient ruins. 2. Santa Elena is a small, beautiful and hot town in the South of Venezuela. How is Santa Elena? It is not big or cold. 3. We live in a tiny and cozy town near the borders. Where do you live? I live in a tiny and cozy town but it is not quite.
TO CONSIDER 1. Adjectives come before the object, place or people they describe. 2. They can also be after one verb: My house is beautiful (mainly after To Be). 3. Adjectives do not change because of gender. E.G: She is beautiful / The park is beautiful. 4. Adjectives are not pluralized. E.G: They are talls.❌ They are tall. ✅

We use comparisons when we want to state similarities or differences about people / places / objects / matters etc. Adjectives are used in this topic but they take a new form. Check the following examples.
Statements Questions Negative statements 1. Joe is more attractive than Kalvin Is Joe more attractive than Kalvin? Joe is not more attractive than Kalvin. 2. China is bigger than Japan. 9.sourceText: TO CONSIDER 1. Adjectives can be divided into two groups: / Short (1 or 2 syllables) / Long (2 or more syllables). 2. Short adjectives take the –er + than particles: Joe is taller than Jim. 3.Long adjectives take the more + than particles: It is more expensive here than there. 4.Short adjectives that finish in –y change to I + er: She is prettier than you. 5. There are irregular adjectives: Good – Better than / Bad – Worse than. 6. We use the particles ‘as / as’ to state similarities: Joe is as tall as Jake. 7. There are adjectives who do not receive comparison degrees; those adjective have absolute meaning: This is the final test / Those people are dead. 8. Less + Adjective + than is used to state inferiority between two nouns. E.G. Alex is less determined than his brother. 9. There are three levels of comparison: Superiority , Equality and Inferiority

9.sourceText: TO CONSIDER 1. Adjectives are divided into two groups: / Short (1 or 2 syllables) / Long (2 or more syllables). 2. Short adjectives take the –est particles: Joe is the tallest in his family. 3. Long adjectives take the most particle: It is the most expensive restaurant in the city. 4. 8.sourceText:
Talking about the past can also have two main grammatical aspects to consider. To Be and other verbs.
TO CONSIDER 1. Even in past, the verb to be is an independent verb it can say a sentence, it can make a question or deny by itself. NO AUXILIARY NEEDED 2. IT has two forms in past: Was ( I/ He / She / It) Were ( You / we / you/ They)
To Be verb He was at home yesterday. Was he at home yesterday? They were in the school this morning. Were they in the school this morning?
Other verbs – Auxiliary Introduction John made a cake last night. Did he make a cake last night? I visited my family in Christmas. Did you visit your family? / What did you do in Christmas?
TO CONSIDER The rest of the verbs are dependent. They use the past auxiliary DID. 1. DID works for all the pronouns. 2. Verbs go in simple form when DID is in the sentence. 3. When we talk about actions happening in the past, we need to use the past progressive tense.
TO CONSIDER 1. We use the verb to be as auxiliary. In both forms: was / were. 2. The main verb takes the –ing form as seen in the examples. 3. When is used to connect two ideas; in this case it presents an action that interrupts another one. 4. While is used to state two actions happening simultaneously. 5. Negative forms are wasn’t / weren’t.
Past Progressive tense I was eating when the earthquake started. Were you eating when the earthquake started? They were relaxing at the beach when they gave the tsunami alert. Were they relaxing at the beach when they gave the tsunami alert? He was running fast while the tornado was chasing him. Was he running fast while the tornado was chasing him?
